There is no system to ensure that important healthcare information including recent administration of medicines and the results of physical observations is passed between separate providers of healthcare in the criminal justice system at the time a person is conveyed between the police, the court and the prison.
lack of information transfer between healthcare providers


There is no standard medical records system which can be accessed by each healthcare organisation to ensure the efficient and effective transfer of medical information.
absence of standard medical records system


During the course of the evidence, it became apparent that the HCPs were not using objective and/or consistent criteria to assess the risk of
inconsistent risk assessment



A GP who had seen Mr [name redacted]Tov during his stay at Colnbrook IRC told the jury that he never seen and was not aware of the content of ACDT documents and regarded the document as a custody officer process. He told the Court that it was not customary for healthcare staff to attend or participate in the ACDT process. This puts detainees at risk.
lack of healthcare staff participation in ACDT process


The nurses who gave evidence similarly were uncertain of their role with respect to the ACDT process and had variable accounts of their involvement in the ACDT process. This puts detainees at risk.
uncertainty of nurses' role in ACDT process


The Consultant [name redacted] psychiatrist did not read the ACDT documents. This puts detainees at risk.
failure of consultant forensic psychiatrist to read ACDT documents



Mr [name redacted]Tov expressed that he might save his medication and take as an overdose. There was conflicting evidence as to the rigour of the checks to ensure detainees had swallowed issued medicine at the time of dispensing and the nurses who gave evidence described different practices of observation. Mr [name redacted]Tov was able to collect sufficient codeine ultimately to be able to end his life. This lack of consistency of checks puts detainee's at risk.
inconsistent medication checks allowing overdose



Mr [name redacted]Tov was taken to the Hillingdon Hospital in the late morning following his overdose on the 16th February 2016. At the Hillingdon Hospital an assessment, examination and blood tests were taken. The blood tests indicated renal impairment. An information system TOXBASE is used in emergency departments to provide assistance to clinicians. Toxbase indicates that in renal impairment greater care must be taken in cases of codeine overdose. This was missed.
failure to apply TOXBASE guidance for renal impairment in codeine overdose



During the journey back to the Colnbrook IRC Mr [name redacted]Tov vomited several times. He vomited on his return to the healthcare unit. The nurse on duty was not told by the escorting custody staff and did not ask about any vomiting in the returning minibus. In oral evidence the nurse said that had he known of the vomiting then he would have returned Mr [name redacted]Tov to the hospital for further assessment. He did not know because he did not ask and was not told.
lack of communication about vomiting during transfer
